title: Boston, Plotted | Michael and Allie

header.eyebrow: Plotted course · Fri Jul 24 to Sun Jul 26, 2026
header.sub: A daddy daughter weekend on foot and on the water. Home port: Hyatt Place Seaport District. No car, no museums, no Fenway. Just the harbor, the neighborhoods, and the food.

facts.html: Land 10:20 AM Fri · UA641 · Term B ↗
Fly out 7:24 PM Sun · UA2136 · Term B ↗

days.heading: Day 1 · Friday, July 24
days.course: Arrive by air, enter by sea. Seaport, the Greenway, and dinner in the North End.

legs.titleHtml: Land at Logan, cross the harbor by water taxi
legs.bodyHtml: Step by step: (1) UA641 lands at Terminal B; you're carry-on only, so skip baggage claim entirely and follow signs straight out to Arrivals, Level 1. (2) Walk out to the arrivals curb and board the free Route 66 shuttle; it loops every terminal and ends at the Logan Boat Dock, 5 to 10 minutes. (3) At the dock, call or app-summon an on-demand water taxi (signage at the dock has the operators; boats usually arrive within 10 to 15 minutes, about $20 per person). (4) Tell the captain Fan Pier. Ten minutes across the harbor, skyline the whole way. (5) From the Fan Pier dock, walk 6 minutes: away from the water to Northern Ave, turn left, Hyatt Placesite is at 295.

chips.label: Shuttle + water taxi + walk · about 35 min, no bag wait

legs.tipHtml: This is the trip's opening shot. Allie's first view of Boston should be from the water.

swap.label: Bad weather backup
swap.bodyHtml: Silver Line SL1 bus, curbside at every terminal's arrivals level, free heading into the city, every 10 min. Ride it through the harbor tunnel to the first stop, Silver Line Way, then walk 5 min to the hotel.

legs.titleHtml: Drop bags at Hyatt Place Seaport
legs.bodyHtml: Room likely won't be ready. They'll hold luggage. Change into walking shoes; you'll log 15k steps today without trying.
Bill Barrett's pick, and it's a five minute walk on Fort Point Channel. Picnic tables under the tent, crab legs, lobster roll, and the chowdah Song ordered you to get. Loud, casual, very Boston.

chips.label: Walk · 5 min from hotel

swap.label: Swap
swap.bodyHtml: James Hook & Cosite next door for a faster counter service lobster roll if the Crab has a wait.

legs.bodyHtml: Cross the Seaport Boulevard bridge and follow the Harborwalk north along the water past the aquariumsite to Long Wharf. Jeff Behrens is right: the harbor is the show. Great photo stops the whole way.

chips.label: Walk · 25 min, all waterfront

legs.titleHtml: Faneuil Hall + Quincy Market, quick pass
legs.bodyHtml: Todd's pick. Street performers, the long market hall, grab a drink. It's touristy, so treat it as a 45 minute walk-through, not a destination.

legs.titleHtml: Rose Kennedy Greenway to the North End
legs.bodyHtml: Wander the Greenway's gardens and public art north, then dive into the North End's narrow streets. Hanover and Salem Streets are the spine; the side streets are the charm. This is the original Boston, now the Italian quarter.

chips.label: Walk · 10 min on the Greenway

legs.tipHtml: Mid afternoon move: cannoli at Modern Pastrysite on Hanover. Megan says Modern over Mike'ssite, and she's correct. Cash speeds up the line.

legs.bodyHtml: Check in for real, shower, put your feet up for an hour. Water taxi or a 20 minute walk back.

chips.label: Walk · 20 min
Or water taxi from Long Wharf

legs.bodyHtml: Megan's pick: red sauce Italian with a fun, slightly retro energy, and the outdoor tables she specifically flagged. Chicken parm and a Shirley Temple for the almost 21 year old.

chips.label: Walk or rideshare · 20 min / 8 min

swap.label: Swap
swap.bodyHtml: Massiminossite on Endicott St, Rob Weinhold's pick, quieter and old school. Beth seconded it hard.

legs.map: Tony and Elaine's 111 N Washington St Boston

legs.titleHtml: Evening stroll: Christopher Columbus Park + waterfront lights
legs.bodyHtml: Walk off dinner under the trellis at the waterfront park, then follow the lit Harborwalk home. If you two still have gas, the adirondack swings at The Lawn on Dsite near the hotel glow at night and are exactly the kind of silly that ends a first day well.

chips.label: Walk · 25 min back to Seaport

days.heading: Day 2 · Saturday, July 25
days.course: Beacon Hill and Back Bay for her, the harbor islands for both of you, tapas and a skyline to finish.

legs.bodyHtml: Ride the T into town and start with shakshuka and a halva latte at the Charles Street Tatte. It puts you at the foot of Beacon Hill as the neighborhood wakes up.

chips.label: SL1/SL2 · Silver Line Way to South Station
Red Line · South Station to Charles/MGH

legs.bodyHtml: Gas lamps, brick sidewalks, hidden gardens. Hit Acorn Street early before the crowds; it's the most photographed street in America and Allie will want the shot. Beth called this one, and Jeffrey O'Neill seconded the neighborhood.

chips.label: Walk · the hill is the activity

legs.bodyHtml: Cross Charles Street into the Public Garden. The swan boats are $5, run since 1877, and are gloriously unhurried. Make Way for Ducklings statues on the way out.

Sharon's daughter was obsessed with Back Bay and yours will be too. Eight blocks of shops from Arlington to Mass Ave. Your job is to carry bags and say yes. Beth warned you this won't be your favorite part of the trip; that's how you know it's working.

chips.label: Walk · Newbury runs parallel to the Garden

legs.tipHtml: Two minute detour at Copley: step into the Boston Public Librarysite courtyard. It's free, it's stunning, and it's a library, not a museum, so it doesn't break your rules.

legs.bodyHtml: Keep it easy and outdoors: Stephanie's on Newburysite for classic patio people watching, or Faccia a Facciasite if you want a chicer room. Wherever she points.

legs.titleHtml: Ferry to Georges Island, Boston Harbor Islands
legs.bodyHtml: Robert Nagle's advice, taken: the harbor over the Freedom Trail. T back to Long Wharf and catch the harbor islands ferry out to Georges Islandsite. Explore Fort Warrensite, a Civil War era granite fort with dark tunnels, ramparts, and skyline views back to the city. It reads as adventure, not history homework.

chips.label: Red + walk · Charles/MGH to Long Wharf area
Harbor Islands ferry · 30 min crossing

legs.tipHtml: Check the return schedule when you land on the island. Aim for a boat back around 5:00 to 5:30.

swap.label: Swap
swap.bodyHtml: A 2 to 3 hour afternoon whale watch from Long Wharf if you'd both rather chase humpbacks than forts. Books out on summer Saturdays, so decide by Thursday.

legs.bodyHtml: Allie's swap — you've already got a Barcelona near home, so go for the Boston original. Toro is Ken Oringer's Spanish tapas room in the South End: order in waves. The maíz asado — grilled corn with lime, aioli, and aged cheese — is the one nobody skips, then patatas bravas, gambas al ajillo, and jamón. Loud, buzzy, and exactly her speed.

chips.label: Rideshare · 10 min from Seaport, or Long Wharf

legs.bodyHtml: Lien's bonus rec, deployed at the right hour. Walk 15 minutes from the South End to the Prudential Towersite and ride to the 52nd floor for sunset over the whole city, harbor to the Charles. Sunset is about 8:10; book the 8:00 window and stay for the lights coming up.

chips.label: Walk · 20 min, or a short rideshare

legs.tipHtml: On the walk over, cut past the Christian Science Plaza reflecting pool. At dusk it mirrors the whole skyline.

days.heading: Day 3 · Sunday, July 26
days.course: Quack loudly, dim sum, one last lap of the harbor, then an unhurried run at Logan.

legs.bodyHtml: Joanne Chang's original. The sticky bun is famous for a reason; split one alongside real breakfast. Seven minute walk from the hotel, and you can check flight status over coffee.

chips.label: Walk · 7 min

legs.bodyHtml: The single most repeated recommendation you got, from Jeffrey, Megan, and Adrian. It's a loop: departs from and returns to the Prudential Center (Huntington Ave side)site, about 80 minutes through the city in a WWII style amphibious vehicle, including the moment it drives straight into the Charles River. Pure fun, zero museum content, and the conDUCKtor will absolutely make Allie quack at strangers. Back at the Pru just before noon.

chips.label: Rideshare · 10 min to Prudential, arrive 10:10

legs.tipHtml: Ask to sit near the front for the river entry splash.

legs.titleHtml: Lunch: Sunday dim sum in Chinatown
legs.bodyHtml: Vaibhav vouched for Chinatown, and Sunday is its best day. Fifteen minute walk from the Duck Tour drop-off. China Pearlsite for classic rolling cart dim sum, pointing at whatever looks good, or Gourmet Dumpling House for soup dumplings. Bubble tea on the way out is mandatory for the 20 year old.

chips.label: Walk · 15 min from Prudential

legs.titleHtml: Greenway back, with an optional final cannoli
legs.bodyHtml: Exit through the Chinatown Gate onto the Rose Kennedy Greenway and stroll it north one last time: fountains, carousel, public art. If Friday's Modern Pastrysite run left a mark, the North End is ten minutes further for a boxed half dozen to fly home with.

chips.label: Walk · 20 min, all Greenway

legs.bodyHtml: Back to the Seaport for a slow lap of the Harborwalk at Fan Pier, the adirondack swings at The Lawn on Dsite, or just a coffee facing the water. This is the deliberately empty block; whatever the weekend still owes you, collect it here.

chips.label: Walk · 20 min from North End, 25 from Chinatown

legs.bodyHtml: Grab luggage from the bell desk, water bottles filled, boarding passes on your phones.

legs.titleHtml: Cross back to Logan the way you came
legs.bodyHtml: Reverse Friday: (1) 4:15, walk 6 minutes from the hotel to the Fan Pier dock; call the water taxi 15 minutes ahead so the boat is waiting. (2) Ten minute crossing to the Logan Boat Dock. (3) Board the free Route 66 shuttle at the dock and hop off at the Terminal B sign; carry-on only with mobile boarding passes, so walk straight past check-in to security. (4) You're at security around 4:50, a full 2.5 hours before UA2136's 7:24 departure. Since Logan is new territory, that's real cushion for security, with time left for a relaxed airside dinner.

chips.label: Walk + water taxi + shuttle · about 35 min door to terminal

swap.label: Backup
swap.bodyHtml: SL1 from Silver Line Way runs direct to every terminal, about 25 min. Fares run one way here: free coming from Logan, standard $2.40 fare going to it. Tap a contactless card or phone when boarding.

checklist.heading: Before you fly
checklist.lede: Six bookings, in the order they'll sell out. Tap to check off.
items: Duck Tour, Sunday 10:30 AM · Prudential departure, 2 seats. Grab it before it goes too. Book tickets ›
View Boston, Saturday ~8:00 PM · timed sunset tickets for 2. Book tickets ›
Toro South End, Saturday 6:30 PM · table for 2. Reserve › Call
Tony & Elaine's, Friday 6:45 PM · ask for outdoor seating. Reserve › Call
Harbor Islands ferry, Saturday afternoon · round trip to Georges Island, or swap to a whale watch and book that instead. Ferry tickets ›
Water taxi on demand · Boston Harbor water taxis run on call when you land. Call 617-406-8584 Get the app ›
checklist.notes: Good to know: Late July runs warm and humid; the harbor legs are the built in air conditioning. Allie is 20, so this plan keeps everything all ages: restaurants yes, bars no, which is why Tall Ship Boston didn't make the cut. Sunday is padded on purpose: at Logan by ~4:50 for a 7:24 flight, since it's your first time in that airport. Checkout is likely noon, so drop bags with the bell desk Sunday morning before the Duck Tour. Everything here is walk, boat, or one T ride, exactly as ordered.

packing.heading: Pack light — carry-on only
packing.lede: Two bags, no checked luggage. Tap to pack.
items: Broken-in walking shoes — you two will log 15k+ steps a day
Light layers + a packable rain shell for the harbor breeze
Sunglasses, a hat, and sunscreen (July sun bounces off the water)
Portable battery pack + charging cables
Refillable water bottle each
Any meds, plus a few blister bandages — moleskin saves the trip
IDs and a card or two; boarding passes saved on your phones
A packable tote for Newbury St finds and a boxed half-dozen cannoli
One nicer outfit each for dinners (Tony & Elaine's, Barcelona)

optional.heading: Optional detour · Cambridge
optional.lede: One extra idea, with my honest take on whether to bother.

cards.bodyHtml: The easy version of a Boston classic: take the Red Line from Park Street or South Station straight to Harvard (about 20 minutes). Walk into Harvard Yard, rub the toe of the John Harvard statue for the photo, then duck into the Harvard Coopsite for a crimson hoodie. Wander Harvard Square — bookstores, buskers, and cafés — and grab burgers at the gloriously dorm-room-y Mr. Bartley'ssite, right across from the Yard. Time permitting, stroll to the Charles River. Red Line back — budget 3 to 4 hours door to door.

chips.label: Red Line · Park St to Harvard, about 20 min
Walk · the Square is compact

cards.tipHtml: The free student-led Harvard Yard tour is genuinely good but needs advance sign-up and caps at five people — otherwise grab Harvard's free self-guided-tour app and go at your own pace.
cards.verdictHtml: My take · Worth it as a swap, not an add-on — this weekend is already full. If Allie's curious about the college-town vibe, or Saturday's harbor-islands weather turns, trade the Georges Island ferry for this. Otherwise I'd keep the harbor; it's the soul of the trip.
